profile.reading: Per H5 Data Centers own site, this Cleveland, Ohio facility sits at 1625 Rockwell Ave and totals 351,000 square feet, built to Tier III colocation standard with 2N UPS power and 2N backup generators rated for 48 hour diesel runtime. The page does not state a power capacity in MW. The facility offers access to 23 on-net carriers and the CL-IX, FD-IX, and Ohio IX internet exchanges, and is SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS compliant, with a 100 percent sales and use tax abatement under an Ohio incentive program.

reading.body:
H5 Data Center in Cleveland occupies 351,000 square feet but its power capacity remains unstated, making the facility's actual compute ceiling unknowable from available sources.

The facility meets Tier III colocation standards with redundant UPS and generator backup rated for 48 hours of diesel runtime. It connects to 23 on-net carriers and three internet exchanges, positioning it as infrastructure for tenants rather than a captive data center. The omission of megawatt capacity is the critical gap. Without power specifications, the building footprint alone does not indicate whether this facility serves regional workloads, hyperscaler overflow, or enterprise colocation. Many colocation providers publish power density; the absence here suggests either limited capacity or incomplete disclosure.

The 100 percent sales and use tax abatement under Ohio incentive law indicates state-level competition for data center investment. This reduces operating costs but does not change the constraint: power supply determines utilization, not physical space or tax incentives. A 351,000 square foot building generates no compute value if its power budget sits idle. The research note flags this as a complete reading as of September 2026, meaning the power capacity either does not exist in public sources or H5 Data Centers has chosen not to publish it.
